resources.string: Rate each area of your life from 1 to 10 as it is today, not as it should be. There are no wrong answers.
Where a goal will help most
The lowest areas. Even one small goal here can lift the whole wheel.
Tap a check to compare it with the wheel above.
Imagine three different versions of your next five years. Don’t look for the right one: each is a real possibility.
Where does what you’re doing now lead in five years? Picture it in detail.
Your current path is suddenly closed. What would you do instead?
Money, status and other people’s opinions don’t matter. How would you live?
Work, home, people, what you learn
Life %d scores highest. Scores aren’t a verdict, though: notice which life you keep thinking about.
The sketch and its ratings will be deleted.
Write down 25 things you want, big and small. Then pick the five that matter most.
Start the list. Anything you want counts: in work, in life, for yourself.
Tap the star next to a goal to pick it for the five.
The five are full. Remove a star first.
Tap the star to pick a goal for the five.
These aren’t a backup list. They matter just enough to steal time from the five, so leave them alone for now.
It will be removed from the list.
Write down what you dream of and put a price on it. Many dreams turn out to cost less than they seem.
Things: a guitar, a flat by the sea, a good bike
Who you want to be: fluent in Spanish, a great cook
Experiences: see the northern lights, run a marathon
One-off costs spread over %d months, plus monthly ones, plus 30%% for the unexpected.
The same amount divided by 30: what each day needs to bring in.
No dreams here yet. Add the first one, even if it seems out of reach.
It will be removed from the list.

These two will suit you best
While the goal itself isn’t clear, a method won’t help. These tools help you find what you really want.
If you tend to give up or put things off, WOOP prepares an if-then plan for exactly that moment.
A clear wording comes first. SMART turns a vague wish into a goal you can check.
A long road has many places to stumble. A pre-mortem finds them in advance.
On a long road it helps to remember why you set out. Five whys find the real reason.
